newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean minister denies interest rate remarks.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean minister denies interest rate remarks.

text.p: South Korean finance minister Kang Kyong-shik denied a newspaper report that he said interest rates should be lowered to between six and seven percent in the medium to long term, ministry spokesman Kim Kyo-shik said on Friday.
"Minister Kang said he never made such remarks," Kim said.

The Chosun Ilbo Friday edition, seen on Thursday night, quoted Kang as saying: "In order for our economy and the finance industry to gain competitiveness, our interest rates should be cut to six to seven percent."
Ministry officials said interest rates were set by market forces and not by the government.
